TakeDamageSfxType.rationale: Presentation only, per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster stream) and monster_state_machine guards N2/N5. DamageSfxType.Armor.

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: Presentation only, per SHARED-FINDINGS section 4 (monster stream) and monster_state_machine guards N2/N5. The whole override body is `if (TestMode.IsOff) { FabricatorNormal.SetBotFallPosition(NCombatRoom.Instance.GetCreatureNode(Creature)); }` -- SetBotFallPosition (FabricatorNormal.cs:60-68) writes a Node2D's Position so the bot drops in from the right height. Read to the END before deciding, per the KinPriest N6 precedent: there is no mechanical statement in it at all. The sim has no override and needs none.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Guardbot.cs:38-45 is one MoveState('GUARD_MOVE', GuardMove, new DefendIntent()) whose FollowUpState is itself, initial state the same node. fabricator.py:36-39 is identical, id included, with Intent(MoveType.DEFEND). No branch state, so no AddBranch argument to misread and no MonsterAi draw on either side (a MoveState's GetNextState is deterministic, monster_state_machine step 10).

guards.what: GuardMove's target set: C# iterates Enemies with NO IsAlive filter (Guardbot.cs:51), the sim filters `not enemy.is_gone` (fabricator.py:47-49)
guards.issue: Guardbot.cs:51 is `Creature.CombatState.Enemies.Where(c => c.Monster is Fabricator)` -- membership of Enemies is the only test, and a creature whose removal was vetoed (Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath, the death-is-not-removal case the stream prompt names) STAYS in Enemies at 0 HP and would still be handed 15 block. The sim's enemies list retains every corpse, so the port has to filter, and it filters on `is_gone` = `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:43-46) -- which also excludes the retained corpse C# would include. Same mechanism, same verdict, at monster/queen's _burn_bright teammate loop (governing rule 3). DORMANT, and the trigger is concrete: no ported power or relic sets `retained_after_death` on a Fabricator (the three sim implementers of should_die are IllusionPower / SteamEruptionPower / AdaptablePower, none of which any Glory monster applies), and the Fabricator's own death ends the fight anyway because every bot carries MinionPower. Note that the sim's filter is the RIGHT shape for the ordinary case -- dropping it would hand block to ordinary corpses -- so this is a missing third state, not a wrong one.

guards.rationale: CreatureCmd.GainBlock(item, 15m, ValueProp.Unpowered, null) (Guardbot.cs:54) vs BlockCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, enemy, 15, props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED) (fabricator.py:49). Amount, recipient (every Fabricator, not the Guardbot) and the Unpowered prop all match. Unpowered matters: monster_state_machine's siblings aside, it is what keeps Vambrace/Pael's Legion multiplicative block modifiers off a monster move, and the sim carries the same prop.

guards.what: Rule 29 -- Guardbot is NOT the same shape as its three siblings
guards.rationale: Read on its own merits rather than inherited: Guardbot alone has no constructor-applied power (contrast Zapbot's HighVoltage 2), no attack, and no debuff, and its AfterAddedToRoom is the pure-visual one that Noisebot and Stabbot share but Zapbot does NOT (Zapbot.cs:29-38 is `async` and appends a real PowerCmd.Apply after the same visual block). Its HP range 16/20 also differs from the other three bots' 18/23.

Guardbot has no encounter of its own: it exists only as a Fabricator spawn (Fabricator.cs:31-35 defenseSpawns, fabricator.py:115), and 'fabricator' is in Glory's normal_keys (rooms.py:189). Spawn mechanics (exactly-one roll, the zero-roll rows) are monster_state_machine steps 47-48 and are NOT re-verdicted here; only the spawn's CONTENT is, and that is monster/fabricator's guard.
